General Nutritional Management of Malabsorption
As with all nutritional disorders, a thorough nutritional assessment is needed to plan rational therapy of malabsorption. Important
historical points to review include duration of symptoms, underlying etiology of malabsorption, ability to meet nutritional needs
by mouth, presence of food allergies, and concurrent medical and surgical problems. The patient's nutritional status (weight, height,
body mass index, and their respective percentiles) should be determined. Tests of body composition such as arm anthropometrics,
bioelectrical impedance, or DEXA scan should be considered. If the underlying cause of malabsorption is not known, diagnostic
gastrointestinal endoscopy, laboratory studies, and/or imaging studies are indicated.
